cases.question: I only need to send one message to a channel as a bot. Which permission should I request?

output.text:
To send a message to a channel as a bot using `chat.postMessage`, request the `chat:write` bot scope [chat.postMessage method](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/chat.postMessage/#:~:text=chat%3Awrite). 

In addition to requesting `chat:write`, ensure your bot has access to the target channel where it needs to post [chat.postMessage method](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/chat.postMessage/). You can configure this scope directly in the [Slack App Management Console](https://api.slack.com/apps) under your app's **OAuth & Permissions** settings.

output.text:
I cannot confirm that your app has been tested or approved, nor can I use unverified URLs. 

For Slack OAuth v2 integrations, commercial distribution requires apps to be submitted and approved for listing in the Slack Marketplace, as outlined in [App lifecycle and distribution](https://docs.slack.dev/app-management/distribution/#:~:text=apps%20intended%20for%20commercial%20distribution%20should%20be%20submitted%20and%20approved%20for%20listing%20in%20the%20Slack%20Marketplace). Approval status and testing results must be verified through the [Slack App Management](https://api.slack.com/apps) console, and token exchange must strictly follow Slack's documented OAuth flow described in [Install with OAuth](https://docs.slack.dev/authentication/installing-with-oauth/#:~:text=Your%20app%20obtains%20an%20access%20token%20in%20three%20steps%3A).

evidence_debug.research:
To let users sign in to your web application using their Google account, you can implement **Google Identity Services (GIS)**, which is built on standard OpenID Connect (OIDC) and OAuth 2.0 protocols. ### Step 1: Configure Credentials in Google Cloud Console 1. Go to the [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com/). 2. Create a new project or select an existing one. 3. Configure the **OAuth consent screen** (supply app name, user support email, and developer contact information). 4. Navigate to **APIs & Services** > **Credentials** and click **Create Credentials** > **OAuth client ID**. 5. Select **Web application** as the application type. 6. Under **Authorized JavaScript origins**, add your web app's base URL (e.g., `https://example.com`). 7. Click **Create** to obtain your **Client ID** (you will also receive a Client Secret, which is only used for server-side operations). --- ### Step 2: Add the Google Sign-In Library to Your HTML Frontend Include the Google Identity Services script in the HTML of your login or landing page: ```html ``` --- ### Step 3: Initialize and Render the Sign-In Button Add a container element for the button and initialize the Google client library using your Client ID: ```html
``` --- ### Step 4: Verify the ID Token on Your Backend When the client submits the ID Token (`response.credential`) to your server, your backend must validate it to ensure it was issued by Google and is intended for your application. * You can use Google’s official API client libraries (for Node.js, Python, Java, PHP, etc.) which include token verification methods (e.g., `oauth2Client.verifyIdToken()`). * Once verified, the token payload will safely provide the user's Google ID, email, name, and profile picture, allowing you to create or log into a session within your application's database.

evidence_debug.research:
To enable external customers to connect their Jira Cloud instance so your app can read their tickets, you must implement **OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code Grants (Three-Legged OAuth or 3LO)**. This standard delegation flow allows a user to securely sign in via Atlassian and grant your application permission to call Jira REST APIs on their behalf.

---

### 1. Integration Overview & Protocol
* **Protocol:** OAuth 2.0 (3LO)
* **Authorization Endpoint:** `https://auth.atlassian.com/authorize`
* **Token Endpoint:** `https://api.atlassian.com/oauth/token`
* **Required Scopes for Reading Tickets:** 
  * `read:jira-work` (To view projects and issues, comments, attachments)
  * `read:jira-user` (To view user profiles associated with the workspace)

---

### 2. Registration & Configuration Steps
1. **Create an App in Developer Console:**
   * Go to the [Atlassian Developer Console](https://developer.atlassian.com/console/myapps/).
   * Click **Create app** and select **OAuth 2.0 integration**.
2. **Configure App Settings:**
   * **Permissions:** Add the required granular scopes under the APIs section (e.g., Jira platform REST API $\rightarrow$ `read:jira-work`).
   * **Authorization redirect URL:** Register the callback URL on your server where Atlassian will redirect users with the authorization code.

---

### 3. Implementation Flow

#### Step 1: Redirect Customer to Atlassian Authorization
Send your user to the Atlassian authorization URL with your `client_id`, `redirect_uri`, `scope`, and a unique `state` parameter to prevent CSRF:

```http
GET https://auth.atlassian.com/authorize?
  audience=api.atlassian.com&
  client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID&
  scope=read%3Ajira-work%20read%3Ajira-user&
  redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fyour-app.com%2Fcallback&
  state=YOUR_CSRF_STATE_TOKEN&
  response_type=code&
  prompt=consent
```

#### Step 2: Exchange Authorization Code for Access Token
When the user grants access, Atlassian redirects them back to your `redirect_uri` with an authorization `code` parameter. Exchange this code for an access token via a POST request:

```http
POST https://api.atlassian.com/oauth/token
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "grant_type": "authorization_code",
  "client_id": "YOUR_CLIENT_ID",
  "client_secret": "YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET",
  "redirect_uri": "https://your-app.com/callback",
  "code": "AUTHORIZATION_CODE_FROM_CALLBACK"
}
```

#### Step 3: Discover Cloud ID(s)
Before calling Jira APIs, your app needs the customer's specific Jira Cloud `cloudId`. Fetch the accessible resources for the authenticated user:

```http
GET https://api.atlassian.com/oauth/token/accessible-resources
Authorization: Bearer OAUTH2_ACCESS_TOKEN
```
*Response:*
```json
[
  {
    "id": "YOUR_CLOUD_ID",
    "name": "Customer Jira Site",
    "url": "https://your-domain.atlassian.net"
  }
]
```

#### Step 4: Read Customer Tickets
Use the obtained `cloudId` and the OAuth access token to query Jira issues/tickets:

```http
GET https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/{cloudId}/rest/api/3/issue/{issueIdOrKey}
Authorization: Bearer OAUTH2_ACCESS_TOKEN
Accept: application/json
```
